agents.name: Tactical Action Officer
agents.description: You command the Navigation picture. Six C# lookouts (Collision Avoidance, Weather Routing, Track Keeping, Self-Defense, Launch Control, Undersea Warfare) report alerts with ready-made options and their predicted results. You choose; the lookout carries out your choice and Bridge Warden checks it against the rules first. Ship survival first (inbound weapons, then collision), then the fight, then weather, then the schedule.

agents.name: Collision Avoidance
agents.description: C# lookout. Watches every non-hostile contact's closest point of approach. When one will pass under 1 nm within 30 minutes it reports, with turn options (right turns first, per the Rules of the Road) and speed options, each with its predicted closest approach.

agents.name: Weather Routing
agents.description: C# lookout. Watches the weather radar, wind and visibility. Heavy weather ahead: turn or slow-down options with the predicted clearance. Fog: safe-speed options (Rule 19).

agents.name: Navigation (Track Keeping)
agents.description: C# lookout. When nothing threatens the ship it offers the return to the planned route and the 16-knot schedule, but only when the way back is clear of ships and heavy weather.

agents.name: Targeting & Launch
agents.description: C# lookout. When a surface track is classified HOSTILE, inside Harpoon range, with nothing in flight at it, it offers return fire (1 or 2 Harpoons) or holding fire. Never at SUSPECT or UNKNOWN tracks.

agents.name: Self-Defense & EMCON
agents.description: C# lookout. Inbound missiles: fight-and-evade, fight, or soft-kill packages (SM-2, ready defenses, General Quarters, a hard turn at speed). SUSPECT or HOSTILE track: EMCON and General Quarters. Picture clear: stand down.

agents.name: Undersea Warfare
agents.description: C# lookout. Torpedo in the water: the run-away heading at the speed that outruns it, the Nixie decoy and General Quarters. Submarine: Nixie and GQ, plus ASROC when it is HOSTILE and in range.

agents.name: Engineering Officer of the Watch
agents.description: You command the Ship Systems picture. C# lookouts (Electrical Plant, Engine Health, Energy) report alerts with ready-made options and their predicted results: breaker re-routes, bringing the standby generator on line, patch cables (casualty power) rigged by a repair team, speed for engine health. You choose; the lookout carries out your choice and Bridge Warden checks it first. Keep vital equipment powered (steering and shafts first, then the radar cooling and the defenses), never overload a generator, protect the engine, fuel last.

agents.name: Electrical Plant
agents.description: C# lookout. Equipment without power: breaker re-routes (each checked for generator overload), the standby generator, or a patch cable (casualty power) rigged by a repair team. Overloaded generator: load-sharing options. Repairs done: back to the normal lineup.

agents.name: Engine Health
agents.description: C# lookout. Engine above its warning temperature: the speed that brings it back under the limit, and a slower step that keeps it under the damage limit.

agents.name: Energy Optimizer
agents.description: C# lookout. Above 20 knots with no threat on any picture: back to the 16-knot schedule to save fuel.

agents.name: Damage Control
agents.description: C# lookout. Each casualty with no team: the nearest manned repair teams with their transit times (and General Quarters if it is not set). No team manned: General Quarters.

agents.name: Damage Control Officer
agents.description: You command the Damage Control picture. The C# Damage Control lookout reports each casualty without a team, with the repair teams that can go and how long each takes. You choose; the lookout sends the team and Bridge Warden checks it first. Fires and floods first (they spread), the nearest manned team, General Quarters when no team is manned.
